page: Amazon Web Services m8g.metal-48xl is a bare-metal general-purpose server powered by AWS Graviton processors. It features 192 physical cores on the arm64 architecture, utilizing the AWS Neoverse-V2 CPU model based on the ARMv9 family. The processor operates at a clock speed of 2.7 GHz with a dedicated core allocation and single thread per core. The system is equipped with 768.0 GB of DDR5 memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. There is no local NVMe storage or GPU acceleration included in this configuration, and network connectivity is supported by a 50 Gbps baseline bandwidth.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier multi-core performance and memory bandwidth. The server achieves top-tier status in stress-ng multi-core CPU tests and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, with read-only cached small block speeds reaching 10,692.66 GB/sec and uncached large block write speeds at 425.8 GB/sec. It also registers top-tier results in database operations, static web serving throughput at 136.65 GB/sec, and Redis SET operations at 360.85 million operations per second. However, single-core performance is moderate, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the average category.

The lack of hyperthreading and specialized vector extensions like AVX or AMX limits certain high-performance computing tasks, and LLM text generation speeds are weak, particularly for small and large models. However, the high physical core density and DDR5 memory subsystem offer strong qualitative cost efficiency for highly parallelized workloads. This server is suited for large-scale database deployments, static web serving, software compilation, and multi-threaded data processing tasks.
